title: SEEKING JUSTICE IN AN UNJUST SYSTEM

sense.text:
Our people have been seeking justice for decades, for centuries, marching and crying no justice, no peace, and seeking it from an unjust system. There will be no justice until Christ returns. Neither can we take it into our own hands and say, let us go get justice for ourselves: we are not forming a military to fight for justice, and we are not forming a justice league on this earth. When our King returns there will be justice. Don’t expect to get justice from this unjust system.

The reason is here: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.” All the curses come upon Israel and overtake us, to destroy us.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”: the curses are a sign, like a street sign or a restaurant sign, so that you can identify who the Israelites are today. We identify who the Israelites are through these curses. That is our genetic marker.

And a wonder, for us to wonder why these things keep happening to us, “and upon thy seed for ever.”

“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships.” Egypt here means the house of oppression, the house of bondage, being kept in oppression. The Hebrew name is Mizraim, and it means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation and distress. So the Lord would bring us again into tribulation, into a place of distress and affliction.

But this time we would go there on ships, cargo slave ships. That took place in the 1600s in the transatlantic slave trade. It happened many times in history, but the last one and the biggest one that we all know about is the transatlantic slave trade.

“Thou shalt see it no more again”: Moses makes it plain that he is not talking about ancient Egypt. You were not going to see ancient Egypt again as slaves.

“And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”: slave men and slave women. That is a curse that fell on the Israelites, a genetic marker for you to know who they are today.

“And no man shall buy you.” To buy here means to redeem. No man will redeem us. The only one that came that could redeem us is Christ.

When we are in the land of our captivity, the land of distress and tribulation, kept in oppression in that spiritual Egypt, “thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness.” At noonday the sun is high in the sky and you are supposed to see clearly, but you are groping. That is our people today. Our people are blind and asleep, going into Christianity, going into being Muslims. We don’t even know who we are as a nation.

“And thou shalt not prosper in thy ways.” All week other nations were talking crap about our people: you black people are uneducated, you don’t go to school, why don’t you open your own business. But we do not fail to prosper because we are illiterate, dumb, stupid people. It means that when we try doing things and we are prospering, people come and destroy it. Tulsa, Black Wall Street: we were prospering, and the white man came and bombed the hell out of us and destroyed it. We had our own banks, and they came and took that. Anytime our people try prospering, Esau comes in and destroys us.

The same in Africa. The system set up over there keeps Nigeria and all our people over there impoverished. Africa is supposed to be rich, but the white man has the IMF, he destabilizes it, and all of a sudden there are terrorists all over Africa. Our enemies create conditions to keep us beneath them, so that we do not prosper.

Wilmington, North Carolina proves it. Black people were in government there, the police chief and city councilmen were black, black businesses were prospering and were competition to the white establishments. The white men felt threatened, and a white militia rose up, killed our people, and took over the government, and nobody ever paid for it. Anytime we prosper we become a threat to them, and they do the same thing today: when there are many black politicians in the Senate and the House, they feel threatened and redraw the districts.

“And thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore.” In these lands we will always be oppressed. There will always be injustice against us, and we will never get justice until our King, our Lord returns. That is why our people keep marching, saying we are men, no justice, no peace, and the oppression never stops. They only replace one thing with the next: after slavery, Jim Crow and the black codes; then the dividing of the houses and redlining, getting the father out of the house; then crack in the community and the war on drugs. The rap music they push in America is oppression too: celebrities are paid to keep us in the midst of sin, to keep their prisons full.

That is a curse that fell upon the twelve tribes of Israel. This is how we know who they are: wherever they are on this earth, they will always be oppressed and spoiled.

precepts.why:
“Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave?” A homeborn slave is born in captivity, and his mind is a mind of servitude. When you are born in captivity your mind does not think about freedom; you have the mind of a slave.

That is Israel, because right through history we have been in captivity after captivity. The Assyrian captivity; then the Hamitic Babylonians had us in slavery; after them the Persians and the Medes; then the Greeks enslaved us; then the Romans subjugated us, destroyed Jerusalem and exiled us from that land, and we fled to Africa and other parts of the world. Then in the 1400s Britain, Spain and Portugal came and enslaved us again. Every nation that rises up and rules this earth puts the children of Israel under subjugation, under slavery.

This last slavery destroyed who we are. All the other nations enslaved us, but they never took our nationality. The white man did the worst to us: he took our nationality, and we no longer know who we are.

“Why is he spoiled?” That is the curse of Deuteronomy 28:29, that we shall be only oppressed and spoiled evermore: we will always be enslaved, we will always be oppressed.

This is why we cannot find justice in an unjust system. “And I will set my face against you”: God sets his face against us when we break his laws. “And ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you.”

The people that hate us are the ones that teach us religion, the ones that set up the court system and the laws, the ones governing over us. If the people that hate you are ruling over you, you are not going to get justice from them. The white man hates negroes and he is ruling over us. He set up this court system, so there is no way you can get any justice in it. Racism is built into the DNA of America: this system was built on racism and injustice.

The history shows it. George Stinney, a fourteen-year-old boy weighing ninety pounds, was accused under Jim Crow of killing two white girls with no evidence, convicted by an all-white jury in ten minutes and put to death in the electric chair, and then Hollywood made The Green Mile, a fantasy with a big strong man in his place. Mary Turner, in 1918, was lynched while pregnant, her stomach cut open and her baby stomped. Lena Baker was tried and sentenced to death within four hours by an all-white jury in 1945, and Georgia admitted she was wrongfully convicted sixty years later. A jury of your peers is supposed to be justice, but an all-white jury is not a jury of your peers. Recy Taylor was raped by white men in 1944; they confessed, and the grand jury refused to indict them. Alabama gave an apology decades later, and our people accept it: you don’t want God’s justice, you want an apology.

Two little black girls, six and four years old, were lynched in Georgia in 1884, and no one was arrested. Sam Hose was lynched before thousands, his ears and fingers cut off and burned alive while the crowd cheered, and pieces of his bones sold as souvenirs. Lynching was like a picnic for them, and then they turn around and say black people are violent. Seventeen-year-old Jesse Washington was burned alive in Waco while the mayor and the chief of police watched. Senators tried to pass an anti-lynching bill again and again, that is the judicial system saying, let us stop being barbaric and lynching, and they said, no, we love lynching niggas. Not one person was ever prosecuted for a lynching. Nine black boys on a train in 1931 were sentenced to death on the word of two white girls, and even after one of the girls admitted she made up the whole story they were still found guilty, and together they served over a hundred and thirty years for a crime they did not commit. In Wilmington the mob murdered our people and took over the government; they call it a race riot, but it was no race riot, it was racist white men murdering our people, and America never paid for it. Black Wall Street in Tulsa was bombed from the air. There was never justice for any of it, and the white man never paid for it. But the Most High God is going to bring forth justice.

And it is not only the past. They are trying to erase that history from the schools because they don’t want to hear it, and what happened in the past is going to happen again. A police officer was recorded punching a woman like a man. They that hate thee are ruling over you; that is why they treat our people like that, why they don’t care if a fourteen, fifteen or seventeen-year-old is put to death or put in jail for life. Our life is worthless in their sight.

sense.text:
“Because ye despise this word”: we despise God’s word. “And trust in oppression”: everything the history shows is oppression, yet our people still trust in that judicial system and in their religions. All those systems set up in slavery are oppressive systems: the slave master court system, the slave master religion. We think we are going to get justice from an unjust system. We march for years, we marched even last Monday, no justice, no peace, and nothing changed. All that changed is that they made some negroes millionaires and allowed some to live in their neighborhoods.

“And perverseness, and stay thereon”: and you stay in it. Our people trust in oppression and stay there.

All these people marching trust in this unjust system. It is our job to teach our people that you cannot trust in oppression: you have to come out of this oppressive system and stop worshipping their god.

This is how God said we should deal with these things. Under the law, if you killed someone accidentally, there were cities you could flee to and live. That is manslaughter.

“Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly”: you were not trying to kill him, but it happened and he is dead. You got into a fight, you got jumped, you had a weapon and you stabbed; you can stab someone in the wrong place, that one vital point, and that is it. You can even kill someone with a punch in the wrong place.

“Whom he hated not in time past” is the key. You did not carry something toward that person and plan it: he did this to me, I’m going to stab him or shoot him when I see him. It was not premeditated, and you had no hatred toward that person in the past.

“As when a man goeth into the wood with his neighbour to hew wood, and his hand fetcheth a stroke with the axe to cut down the tree.” That is righteous judgment, God’s judgment: if you kill someone and it was not premeditated, the judgment should not be stiff. It should not be death; your life should not be taken away, because you never hated that person and your intent was not to kill him.

Karmelo Anthony was under the tent minding his business when white boys came up, surrounded him, punched him and put him in a headlock. He was threatened, he was a small young man, and he pulled out a knife and defended himself, and the boy died. Under Texas law, if you fear someone is about to do harm to you, you can defend yourself. When people are scared, that is when they are most dangerous. The family of the boy who was bullying him feels it too, so you have to be careful with things like that. But it was self-defense, or at most manslaughter, and they charged it as capital murder and gave him thirty-five years.

precepts.why:
“Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment”: if you are righteous, you cannot do unrighteousness when it comes to judgment. A life was still lost, so righteous judgment might be three years, even five years. But thirty-five years for manslaughter, for defending yourself, is too much. Judgment must be righteous, but you cannot find justice in an unjust system.

“Thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty: but in righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbour.” Respect of persons is partiality, favoritism toward someone because of wealth, social status or appearance rather than their worth or character. If you know a man’s intent was not malice, that it was not premeditated, the judgment should not be so stiff.

There was respect of persons in the Karmelo Anthony verdict. Others did even worse things and were not given thirty-five years. The father and the judge are shown together at Christmas parties; they know each other. If you are friends with the judge and it is an all-white jury, is there partiality there? Yes. The verdict was racially biased. He did take a life, and there are laws for that, but you are not supposed to get the stiff penalty of life in prison. And the Lord is behind all of that we see taking place.

The same thing happened in Midlothian in 2025: a young black man was jumped by a group of white kids, called hateful names, told a gun was present, and in defending himself he injured one of them, the son of a sheriff’s deputy. They did not drop it as self-defense; they charged him with assault with a deadly weapon. If your son is a bully and gets hurt bullying people, that says a lot about the father, because you are supposed to know what type of person your son is.

And see how they think. A man stood outside the courthouse and said Karmelo Anthony should be swinging from a tree, the way they used to lynch a seventeen-year-old brother in front of the courthouse fifty years ago. He was arrested for terroristic threats, but he will be let go, because the system is always for them. There is word that the Aryan Nation has a hit out on him in jail. If that is true there will be rioting, and that is what the elites want: order out of chaos. They want black people to rise up and pick up guns so they can kill you, change the laws and bring you into subjection. Another says he deserves to rot in prison. The boy’s father calls him a watermelon felon and tells our people a civil war was fought to free them, but the civil war was not to free us. That is why his son saw that black boy under the tent and told him he could not be under their tent. And when a black coworker threw grease in a white boy’s face, which is wrong and he has to go to jail for it, they say we need to kill black people, raise our children to be as violent as they are, and put them back in their place like the white men of the fifties who stepped on them. People are preparing for war; white people are tired of our people and don’t want to share rulership with us, all over the world. What they used to do in the fifties, stepping on us, is what it is coming back to.

sense.text:
“Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad.” Injustice is oppression, and if you are a wise man, it is going to make you angry. Putting this lesson together made me angry: these people look at us as though our life is worthless. And when you look at our people on the internet, all you see is women shaking their ass and dumb stupid stuff. We have to change.

The culture our people created in America is one of the worst cultures in the world: singing music about killing each other, selling drugs to each other, murdering each other. Esau is behind it. The music industry could say stop singing about killing each other, but that keeps the prisons full and the justice system going. Esau understands that when people are impoverished and put in a certain situation, crime rises. Black people do not commit the most crime; the most crime is committed by white people, it just is not televised. But we are the only ones that glorify dumb stupid stuff, and we have to change our people’s minds and change the way they look at us. The liberals did this to us: they create situations to keep us in sin.

I’m not mad when white people do evil and say evil things; that is in their nature, that is who they are. I’m angry when I see my brothers and sisters doing evil and saying dumb stupid things, giving them bullets to talk crap about our people.

So when you see injustice, you get angry. But when you get angry, you have to use the wisdom of God to help your people come out of that oppression and injustice: to go even harder to teach your people and show them what they have to do to change, for these injustices to stop. It is okay to be angry, but we are not going to join a civil rights movement and march with them. We show our people the solutions.

This is the solution, what we do when we see these things happening. “And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity”: the bread of adversity is injustice, this unjust system, oppression; our people killed in the street, our brothers put in prison at a high rate, the school-to-prison pipeline. “And the water of affliction”: our tears, the tears coming down from mothers’ eyes because of affliction, while they tell us we are not oppressed.

“Yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more.” When our people are being afflicted, that is when the teachers have to rise up. That is how a wise man gets mad: he comes into the school, learns these scriptures, changes his life, and goes and teaches his people. Our job is not to join these groups, and not to hide when these things happen. We have to teach on it and show people why these things are happening: because you trust in oppression, and this system is built on oppression.

“But thine eyes shall see thy teachers”: we have to be out there where they see us, teaching our people why the oppression doesn’t stop, why they keep marching year after year, decade after decade, and there is no justice. We have to show them who their oppressor is and change our people’s minds: the sisters to stop dressing as hoes and acting ratchet, the brothers to stop the gang mentality and change their lives. When we do march, it is not marching for justice, thinking this system will help us. We march to bring awareness, so that their eyes see their teachers, and after every march we set up and teach and tell our people to repent.

“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it”: what our people are supposed to hear is, you are Israelites, keep God’s commandments, change your life, come out of Christianity. This is why you are being oppressed, why you are afflicted, why you are crying.

God brings affliction because that is the only time our people will listen. Many of our people trust in the system the slave master set up and think America is built on justice, so God has to show you that this system is not going to help you. As the white man reveals himself to you, it is up to us to come in and tell you what God says: this is the way, walk ye in it. We are not to follow them when black people get mad and march; let them follow us. “When ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.”

“Ye shall defile also the covering of thy graven images of silver, and the ornament of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away”: our people will change. But first the affliction has to happen, and when it does, the teachers go out on the highways and byways and tell them, this is the way. God has a purpose behind everything he does, even what happened with Karmelo Anthony.

precepts.why: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart”: God gives leaders, teachers after his heart, “which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.” They teach you knowledge of who you are and understanding of the scriptures. They tell you that you are the Israelites and you have to keep God’s commandments. Those are the teachers no longer removed into a corner.

“Moreover this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of God”: our people have erred in the knowledge of God. “But whereas they lived in the great war of ignorance”: our people live in ignorance, and there is a war going on, and that war is to keep black people ignorant and stupid.

“Those so great plagues called they peace”: the oppression and the affliction, and they call that peace. A plague is worshipping a god that doesn’t look like you. You cannot say you are against white supremacy and racial injustice and yet worship your oppressor’s god, your slave master’s god. You support white supremacy when you go to church every Sunday and worship white Jesus, because that religion was used to enslave you and destroy you. What changed from being Christians in the time of the KKK until now? Nothing. How can a white god save you from white man oppression? For over four hundred years you have been praying to that white god, and he has done nothing for you; you are still living in oppression.

Our people out there marching for justice don’t really want justice. God’s justice means a lot of people have to die; God is a righteous judge. When you talk about the kingdom of heaven and justice, they don’t ask about the Chinese or the Arabs; they always ask, what about the white man? That is how dumb and stupid our people are. That is Stockholm syndrome.

Why does God allow these things to happen, a case as plain as Karmelo Anthony’s self-defense ending in thirty-five years? “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face”: God wants us to acknowledge our offense and seek him, to come back to him. We are the children of Israel, the real children of Israel.

“In their affliction they will seek me early.” That is the water of affliction the Lord gives. Things are about to get very, very bad all over this earth because our people don’t want to turn to God. They still worship white Jesus, still idolize the white man as God, follow all these fake religions, and want to party. So God says, I am going to afflict you, and how he is afflicting us is by turning the white man back into who he was in the 1800s and the 1940s and 50s. The white man is changing back into his real nature, and in our affliction we are going to seek him early.

This is the affliction that is going to take place. “Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things”: strait things are hard things. The righteous of our people are going to be oppressed too, and many of us will be killed here in America for teaching the word of God. “And hope for wide”: we hope that the Lord accepts us and we get the kingdom.

“For they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things”: those following Christianity and living wickedly in this world suffer the hard things too. The hard things are affliction and oppression, white people rising up and killing us, putting us in concentration camps. It will not happen to the Israelites alone; it will happen to all black people all over the world, in all the European countries, because the white man hates all black people.

“And yet shall not see the wide”: they suffer the same affliction, yet they do not get the kingdom. The righteous and the unrighteous are going to suffer in America and in Europe. The affliction is coming on Israel as a whole, even in South America, even the northern kingdom.

sense.text:
In their affliction they will seek God early; this is what God wants us to do. “Come out of her, my people.” The her is mystery Babylon the great, and God wants his people to come out of her.

“That ye be not partakers of her sins”: her sins are her religion, her politics, her policies, that whole unjust system. Don’t partake in the sins of America: the false religion, Christianity, worshipping the white man as God. “And that ye receive not of her plagues”: if you partake, you will receive of the plagues that come here too.

precepts.why: Who are God’s people that he calls out of her? “And chariots, and slaves, and souls of men.” God’s people are the slaves that were brought here, the people the merchants of the earth were trading as slaves. And souls of men: souls are being sold here; they sell you that American dream.

Coming out of her does not mean running from the country. It means separating yourself, and when we separate, we have to gather together. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together.”

Gathering together is not just coming together on the Sabbath. Most of us are not going to have Medicaid any more; they are trying to get rid of Medicaid and social security. In the past our people had no doctors or dentists, and the Black Panthers set up programs to help our people. We will have to set up programs to take care of our people. Gathering together is establishing the kingdom of heaven: working together, getting things done on our own, creating farms, learning to be self-sufficient and producing our own food. Right now we are in the beginning of sorrows, and as Christ says, the end is not yet, so we have time to put things together. We all have to be of one mind and really love each other.

The leaders will put things together, mainly for the elderly, the young, the widows and the fatherless; in the end we will not be able to help millions of people. You young, strong brothers, and you sisters that are working and have money now, are supposed to be coming together, setting things up and preparing for what’s coming. Don’t wait until the last minute.

“O nation not desired”: we have to gather together and do things on our own because we are a people not desired. They hate us. Black people, the twelve tribes of Israel, are a hated people, and God says gather together “Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff”: before the Lord brings judgment on this earth.

sense.text: “Measure thou the time diligently in itself”: this is how we know what time we are living in. You have to be able to measure the time.
“The very same time, wherein the Highest will begin to visit the world which he made”: that is the time we are living in right now, when the Lord begins to visit the earth he made.

“Therefore when there shall be seen earthquakes”: there was an earthquake in the Philippines this week. “And uproars of the people in the world”: we are seeing uproars all over the earth right now. The white man is rising up all over Europe and all over America and saying, we don’t want you black people around us any more.

Many think white people have changed, but he is turning into who he really is. A white pastor in Britain says a black man off a boat should not have the same right to vote and take part in running the country as he has. This week in Belfast, after a Sudanese asylum seeker was charged with an attempted beheading, they used it to show how much they hate black people: mobs went door to door, burning down houses where black people and migrants live and beating any black person they saw in the street, and nurses from Uganda fled their home with only their passports. In Italy the Nazi salutes are back. In Texas they say, your replacement is here. And one of the richest men on earth tells white people, you either fight back or you die. Our people are clueless about what is about to take place. When white people get angry, you are going to see who they really are.

“Then shalt thou well understand, that the most High spake of those things from the days that were before thee, even from the beginning.” Seeing the uproars and the civil unrest, we understand that God said from the beginning that these things would happen.

What is going to cause the uproars? Things are about to get very bad: there will be civil war, and many of our people living among white people in Europe and America will die. The last time Europeans turned into their real nature, in World War II, they fought each other and over eighty million people died; this time it is going to be billions. After 1945 they reflected and said, this is some evil we are doing; let us change our image to the world, give the slaves some rights, set up a system of justice and equality, and let the people we oppressed come to our countries. Decades later they say, we should never have allowed any of you in. That is in the scripture.

“And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron.” The fourth kingdom is the one that rules this earth before Christ returns. Babylon; the Persians and the Medes, that is Iran; Greece; and Rome. The fourth kingdom began with Rome, and America and Europe are an extension of Rome: the iron, the feet. “Forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things”: that iron broke in pieces and bruised and subjugated all nations. Rome did it, and America and Europe did the same thing.

“And whereas thou sawest the feet and toes”: the feet and toes are Europe and America. “Part of potters’ clay, and part of iron”: it has clay in it and iron in it. “The kingdom shall be divided”: Europe is divided and America is divided, because they have clay in them and iron in them. “But there shall be in it of the strength of the iron.”

“And as the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay”: the last part of the kingdom is mixed, and iron and clay cannot mix. “So the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.” This system is broken: Europe is broken and America is broken, because the same people they colonized and destroyed, they brought to live among them. Trump is trying to fix the system, and Europe says it is trying to fix the system too, but it is too late.

“They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men”: the clay is the seed of men, and the iron, the white man, mingled himself with all nations. This began after 1945. Britain let anyone from the countries it had colonized come with a British passport to serve and help rebuild the economy, which is why there are so many Indians and Pakistanis there. After civil rights everybody started coming to America; before that America was a racist country, and not everyone could come. The white man said he would change, and he mixed with miry clay.

“But they shall not cleave one to another”: white people and everyone else are not going to get along. That is what you see going on in Europe and in America.

precepts.why:
Why will they not cleave one to another? “Never trust thine enemy.” Who is your enemy? In the 1800s, in the fifties, forty or fifty years ago, you understood who your enemy was. God says never trust him.

“For like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” Remember that the fourth kingdom is made of iron: that iron is white people. Rust will always appear on iron, and that is the white man’s wickedness. For the last fifty years he said he changed: we gave you civil rights, we are not oppressing you any more. But you see his wickedness coming back, because his kingdom is made of iron, and they are taking all those rights back.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: they act like they love black people and care about black people. “Yet take good heed and beware of him”: beware of that iron. “And thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass”: you see all his wickedness. Even though they say they are about justice and rights, they are not showing it. If you are righteous and have wisdom, you understand you can never trust these people. Look at their history: they are a genocidal race of people. Look at Palestine, where hundreds of thousands have died, and Lebanon, and the Congo. Who is bringing forth righteous judgment and justice on this earth? This whole system is unjust.

“And thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” The white man did not change. He is the same person, you are seeing it today, and he doesn’t want black people around him.

sense.text: “A roaring lion chased out of the wood”: that roaring lion, first and foremost, is the spirit of Christ in the prophets, speaking to the eagle. The eagle is the fourth kingdom we read in Daniel 2.
“Hear thou, I will talk with thee, and the Highest shall say unto thee”: the Lord speaking through his prophets.

“Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world”: God made the white man to reign in his world, this fourth kingdom, Europe and America. “That the end of their times might come through them”: they are a genocidal, murderous people. They have created weapons that could destroy everybody on this earth, and they will use them on themselves. That is how the end of their times comes through them.

“And the fourth came, and overcame all the beasts that were past”: they conquered all the nations that were before them, “and had power over the world with great fearfulness, and over the whole compass of the earth with much wicked oppression.” The white man ruled this earth with much wicked oppression; that is how Europe and America rule. “And so long time dwelt he upon the earth with deceit”: acting like he is righteous, a Christian nation. But as we reveal him and show you who he is, his real nature is coming out.

“For the earth hast thou not judged with truth.” They say justice is blind, but the white man does not judge with truth, so we are not going to get justice from this unjust system. And it is not just America: the whole earth he has not judged with truth. Patrice Lumumba and Thomas Sankara were executed and killed because they were against this unjust system. There has never been any justice for that, and the white man has not paid for it yet, but God is going to bring judgment on him for what he has done.
